An implementation that gates on the count and ignores the submission kind therefore passes all nine new scenarios, the ten shipped S1 scenarios and the declared handler table, while sending a secret rotation to the I-14 confirm page - the I-14 words ('Save the new app?') are wrong for a rotation and an already-delivered promise is lost silently, in exactly the state this slice introduces.
findings.remediation: Give F183 an observation and cite it: either add one public scenario - a workspace connected through the saved app, Priya rotates the signing secret with the client secret left blank, she reads 'Saved. Workspace admins can now choose Add to Slack.' on the integrations page and is never taken to the confirm page (reuse then_on_confirm_page's negation or assert the integrations-page answer plus the unchanged client ID) - or add the Rotate-with-connections case to the declared handler table row and list L3/F183 in its obligations. diagnostic: Rejected on one blocking coverage defect; everything else in the S2 oracle is sound. The nine public scenarios drive the real doors, pin the locked I-14 n = 1 line verbatim, close E8-E14 and E22, keep every secret off the confirm page in six encodings, and observe preservation of the current app through page copy, activity population, Add to Slack approval and a signed event verifying with the old signing secret. The RED reused from the root's run at this clean revision is semantic (the different app takes effect at once; the confirm door answers 404) with zero parsing, hook or fixture failures and the ten shipped S1 scenarios still passing, and every step the new scenarios need is defined, including the shared injected clock. Blocking: L3's discriminating case F183 has no falsifier - no cited test submits the same client ID while a workspace is connected, so a gate keyed on the connected count alone passes the entire oracle while sending a secret rotation to the I-14 confirm page and silently losing US-IIS-05 AC 1 / P1 / E3, the promise this slice's new gate sits on top of. Two further oracle findings are non-blocking and do not veto craft once the first is corrected: L4's expiry-instant case F188 and L6's config-version clause have no cited observation. Re-review is limited to the corrected case and the obligations it touches; all other judgments and the reused RED evidence stand. typesafe: unavailable (exit 3, key absent), so the three classifications are reviewer-owned.
